model.name: Legal Instrument / Norm
model.purpose: Represent an authority-backed legal instrument and the norms expressed by its addressable source fragments, independent of storage and interface format.
model.scope_statement: Owns legal-work, expression, manifestation, source, provision and norm linkage; instrument class; authority and legal-basis references; structure and citations; authenticity and provenance; deontic assertions; lifecycle, temporal applicability, interpretation, access and projections. Organizations, lawmaking procedures, cases, enforcement events, affected parties, places and generic document storage remain external masters.
in_scope: Legal work, expression, manifestation, item, authoritative source, provision and norm identity
Authority, class, structure, citation, normative meaning, lifecycle, time, applicability, conflict and provenance
Authentication, consolidation, controlled disclosure, retention, interoperability and safe agent operations
out_of_scope: Issuing organization, legislative or administrative procedure and generic document repository masters
Court or arbitration case, enforcement event, affected person, asset and place masters
Automated legal advice, universally binding interpretation or substantive law common to every jurisdiction

boundary_notes.distinction: Authorities are external organizations referenced in a specific legal capacity; the legal instrument owns neither their identity nor governance.
The process produces adoption and publication evidence; the instrument aggregate preserves outputs and lifecycle assertions but not the workflow master.
A case may interpret, invalidate or apply an instrument, but its parties, procedure, evidence and decision lifecycle remain a separate model.
A policy or rule may lack legal-source authority; this aggregate requires explicit legal-source, jurisdiction and competent-authority bindings.
Files and records are manifestations or evidence items; they do not replace authority-qualified legal-work identity or normative semantics.

sources.title: Akoma Ntoso Version 1.0, Part 1: XML Vocabulary
sources.relevance: Defines source-oriented legal-document structure, metadata, references, identifiers, lifecycle events, modifications and analysis markup for legislation and other legal documents.

sources.title: Akoma Ntoso Version 1.0, Part 2: Specifications
sources.relevance: Specifies naming, identification, references and conformance rules used to preserve addressable legal-document identity across expressions and manifestations.

sources.title: LegalRuleML Core Specification Version 1.0
sources.relevance: Defines formal features for legal norms and rules, including legal sources, authority, jurisdiction, temporal characteristics, deontic effects, defeasibility, exceptions and overrides.

sources.title: What is the European Legislation Identifier
sources.organization: Publications Office of the European Union
sources.version_or_date: Official ELI register page, updated 27 January 2026
sources.relevance: Defines ELI identification, metadata, publication and synchronization pillars and applies work, expression and manifestation distinctions to legislation.

sources.title: ELI Subdivisions Specifications
sources.relevance: Provides persistent identification and metadata guidance for addressable subdivisions such as articles, recitals and annexes.

sources.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
sources.relevance: Provides interoperable provenance for entities, activities, agents, derivation, generation, attribution and qualified responsibility.

sources.title: Time Ontology in OWL
sources.relevance: Provides instants, intervals, temporal relations, duration and alternative temporal-reference systems needed to distinguish legal event and applicability times.

sources.title: SKOS Simple Knowledge Organization System Reference
sources.relevance: Supports governed concept schemes, labels, notation and mappings for instrument type, legal status, subject, jurisdiction and other controlled classifications.

sources.title: Council conclusions inviting the introduction of the European Legislation Identifier
sources.relevance: Establishes the ELI policy basis for URI identification, metadata and machine-readable publication while preserving differences among national legal systems.

sources.title: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Defines machine timestamps with seconds and an explicit UTC offset for legal, publication, observation, knowledge and processing events.

functions.name: Register legal work
functions.description: Create authority-qualified identity, class, master register and initial source binding.
effects: the work becomes resolvable without collapsing its expressions

functions.name: Add expression or manifestation
functions.description: Bind a language expression, file manifestation or held item to the same legal work.
effects: the new representation is separately identifiable and attributable

functions.name: Authenticate authoritative source
functions.description: Record publisher, publication act, authenticity evidence, digest and copy status.
preconditions: publisher role and evidence are known
effects: official and unofficial copies remain distinguishable

functions.name: Address provision and citation
functions.description: Mint or bind stable subdivision identities and resolve static or dynamic citations.
preconditions: source versions and numbering history resolve
effects: provisions stay citable across rendition and renumbering

functions.name: Bind norm to source
functions.description: Attach a structured or formal norm to exact source fragments with author, method and confidence.
preconditions: source fragments and expression version resolve
effects: formal semantics remain attributable and contestable

functions.name: Record legal lifecycle event
functions.description: Append adoption, publication, commencement, suspension, repeal, expiry or correction evidence.
preconditions: competence, affected scope and times validate
effects: state changes without overwriting prior assertions

functions.name: Construct consolidated view
functions.description: Apply cited modifications to create a dated non-authoritative or authority-qualified consolidated expression.
preconditions: all applied sources and unresolved conflicts are explicit
effects: the view remains distinct from original acts

functions.name: Assess applicability as assertion
functions.description: Produce a source-qualified applicability result for stated facts without claiming universal legal judgment.
preconditions: versions, jurisdiction and authority scope resolve
effects: reasoning inputs and unresolved conflicts stay inspectable

functions.name: Issue interoperability view
functions.description: Project a selected legal-work revision to Akoma Ntoso, LegalRuleML, ELI or linked-data form with declared loss.
preconditions: target version and disclosure policy validate
effects: projection links source digest and omissions

functions.name: Retire or supersede legal work
functions.description: Mark expiry, repeal or replacement while preserving citations, versions, sources and successor resolution.
effects: future active use is blocked while history stays citable

composition.purpose: Resolve issuing, adopting, promulgating, publishing and interpreting actors without duplicating their masters.

composition.target: Legislative Process, Court Case, Enforcement Event, Person, Place and Document models
composition.purpose: Connect the instrument to external creation, interpretation, application, party, jurisdiction and storage contexts.
Project legal-document structure, identifiers, references, metadata and lifecycle markup.
Project source-linked formal norms, modalities, temporal characteristics, exceptions and override relations.
Project legal-resource identity, metadata, provenance, time and controlled classifications with explicit version and loss.

owner_package_requirements: Dimension identity, owner, legal-register authority, publication authority and namespace
Legal work, expression, manifestation, provision, norm, lifecycle, citation and interpretation registries
Master-system mappings for authority, instrument, source, case, party, place and event references
Identity, authority, authenticity, temporal, citation, amendment, access, retention and agent-operation policies
dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint legal-work and assertion identifiers only when no authoritative legal register identity exists; keep organizations, procedures, cases, enforcement events, parties, places and generic documents as typed references.
registry_links: Dimension-local legal work, provision, norm, citation, lifecycle and interpretation registries

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize by authority-qualified legal-work identifier and register, never by title, citation, URL, language, text, file, date or digest.
Keep work, expression, manifestation, item, authoritative source, provision, norm and formal rule separately identifiable.
patch_rules: Extensions declare legal-system profile, target finding, source, authority, vocabulary versions, temporal semantics and interoperability impact.
Identity, authority, source anchoring, normative semantics or lifecycle changes require a successor version, migration map and continued resolution of cited history.
compatibility_rules: Unknown additive fields may be ignored only when identity, authority, source, provision addresses, legal times, lifecycle, access and provenance remain intact.
Every Akoma Ntoso, LegalRuleML, ELI or linked-data projection pins versions and states transformed fields, omissions and round-trip limits.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-register identifier for the legal work, qualified by issuing or publishing jurisdiction.
Governed globally resolvable legal-resource IRI with authoritative register binding.
Dimension UUID or ULID when no external identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Use RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and offset or Z; separate adoption, signature, publication, commencement, efficacy, applicability, observation, knowledge and ingestion times.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Use {legal-work-id}--{artifact-kind}--{assertion-or-event-id}; never use title, citation, URL, language, date or hash alone.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, media type, language, publisher, source and profile versions, authority, valid and knowledge times, source anchors, quality, licence and access marking.

policies: Only a competent legal or publication authority may establish canonical source status or authority-qualified lifecycle effect.
Publication, online availability, a formal rule or a consolidated view never alone proves validity, force or applicability.
Agents may extract, validate and propose; amendment, legal-status assertion, final interpretation, wider disclosure and destructive retirement require accountable authority.
Conflicting texts, norms, interpretations and temporal assertions remain separately attributable until resolved by a competent process.

read: Resolve Dimension, legal-system profile, register, authority, work version, expression language, provision address, legal time and access purpose.
create: Create work identity, authority, class, source, expression and explicit unknowns before norms, lifecycle conclusions or projections.
update: Append assertion or event with authority, reason, source fragments, legal and knowledge time and validation; never overwrite cited history.
delete: Apply legal hold and records policy; prefer repeal, expiry, supersession or tombstone and never cascade to authorities, cases, parties or events.

responsibilities: Own canonical work identity, instrument class and authority-qualified lifecycle.

roles.name: Norm formalization reviewer

roles.name: Access and records steward
responsibilities: Apply disclosure, protected-annex, retention and legal-hold policy.

roles.name: Interoperability steward
responsibilities: Validate format mappings, source identity and declared information loss.

access.default_rule: Deny mutation and restricted draft or protected-provision disclosure unless register, role, purpose and field policy grant it; expose only the necessary source and precision.
exceptions: Statutory, judicial, oversight or emergency access cites authority and remains purpose-bound, attributable and reviewable.
audit_requirements: Log actor, agent, role, purpose, legal work, operation, policy, RFC 3339 time, authority, affected source fragments and outcome.

read_order: Read Dimension legal-register, source-authority, temporal, citation, amendment, interpretation, access and retention policies.
Read this model and linked organization, process, case, event, party and place models before mutation.

coverage.claim: Covers a governed legal instrument and its source-linked norms from identity and authority through structure, lifecycle, applicability, provenance and exchange.

checklist.notes: Authority-qualified work identity and separate expression, manifestation, item, source, provision and norm identity are explicit.
Instrument, jurisdiction, subject, status and norm classifications are versioned.
Structure, text anchors, citations, modality, conditions, legal states and integrity properties are first-class.
Authority, authenticity, publication, derivation, verification and confidence evidence are covered.
Register, publish, address, cite, formalize, amend, consolidate, project and retire operations are governed.
Authorities, procedures, cases, enforcement events, parties, places and generic documents retain external masters.
Drafting, adoption, signature, publication, commencement, suspension, repeal, expiry, correction and supersession preserve history.
Citations, amendments, derivations, overrides, exceptions, successors and interpretations are typed and attributable.
Legal event, validity, force, efficacy, applicability, observation and knowledge times remain distinct.
Territorial jurisdiction and place references are covered without importing geographic masters.
Source publication, derivation, attribution, custody, digest and formalization history remain attributable.
Register, publisher, lawmaking, formalization, access and interoperability roles remain separate.
Identity, authority, addresses, citations, time, lifecycle, formalization, access and stale-head checks are explicit.
Public, restricted draft, protected annex and purpose-bound views are covered.
Original sources, amendments, superseded versions, citations and tombstones are preserved.
Akoma Ntoso, LegalRuleML, ELI, PROV, OWL-Time and SKOS projections are loss-aware.

known_omissions: No independent Claude or Grok result was available; later comparative legal and legal-informatics review is required before canonical promotion.
Jurisdiction-specific constitutional hierarchy, legislative procedure, publication law, treaty law, customary law, religious law and multilingual drafting profiles require specialist review.
The frozen relation ledger contains no approved WM-POL-001 rows; all composition targets remain draft.
Certified Akoma Ntoso, LegalRuleML, ELI and linked-data crosswalks, validation fixtures and legal-system profiles remain future work.
conflicts: A legally authoritative instrument source and a formal norm or executable rule are not interchangeable.
Validity, force, efficacy, applicability and publication can disagree for the same work or provision.
Original acts, correcting acts, amendments and consolidated views can expose different text without sharing the same legal authority.
regional_assumptions: ELI is a European interoperability framework and does not define universal substantive law.
Akoma Ntoso and LegalRuleML are representation standards and do not create legal authority or binding interpretation.
A jurisdiction's competent authorities and adopted legal-system profile control legal effect.
adversarial_checks: Reject identity inferred from title, citation, URL, language, text, file or hash alone.
Reject a publication or consolidation represented as binding without competent-authority evidence.
Reject a formalized rule treated as identical to its legal source or as uncontested interpretation.
Reject applicability or conflict resolution that hides facts, provision versions, jurisdiction, time, authority or uncertainty.
Reject destructive amendment or deletion that erases cited source and lifecycle history.
